phase_name: Result/query use cases and command/query boundary

pre_execution_questions.question: Should user intents that read/show existing research results be first-class use cases separate from research commands?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Without this boundary UI/read-side requests get mixed with data collection.

pre_execution_questions.question: Should every future UI screen become a use case?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Screen composition and domain intent are not the same abstraction.

pre_execution_questions.question: Should projection builders become top-level use cases?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Internal implementation capabilities should not inflate the user-intent registry.

pre_execution_questions.question: How do we distinguish “show what changed” from “run research to find what changed”?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Natural-language overlap requires deterministic command/query boundaries.

pre_execution_questions.question: May query use cases mutate research truth or silently trigger refresh/measurement?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Read-side semantics must remain predictable and auditable.

pre_execution_questions.question: Is increasing from 20 to 25 top-level UCs architecturally justified?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: The new capability must not bypass the complexity budget.

pre_execution_questions.question: Are the five result products real backend outputs in Phase 2, or only contracts until Phase 3?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: The release must not overclaim implementation readiness.

emergent_questions.question: Did adding UC21–UC25 change any of the 47 pre-existing v1.10 routing fixtures?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: A new query plane must not regress established command/lifecycle routing.

post_execution_answers.answer: Yes. UC21–UC25 are first-class query UCs representing Current State, Changes, Trend, Interpretation and Research Health.
post_execution_answers.decision: Model read/explain intents separately from command UCs.

post_execution_answers.answer: No. Composite screens such as Direction Detail invoke multiple query UCs and command actions but are not domain use cases.
post_execution_answers.decision: Keep screen composition in UI mapping/System Map.

post_execution_answers.answer: No. Projection builders remain capabilities/internal implementation, not top-level UCs.
Route using action intent plus state hints: existing result/read intent selects UC22; explicit refresh/research intent selects UC09 (and analogous boundaries for other products).
post_execution_answers.decision: Preserve user intent rather than routing by screen wording.

post_execution_answers.answer: No. Query UCs are read-only with writes=[]; missing/stale data is surfaced, not silently repaired by mutation.
post_execution_answers.decision: Refresh remains an explicit command-side action.

post_execution_answers.answer: Yes, because result/query is a genuinely new user-capability class. The budget is explicitly revised to 25 UCs, six groups and five query UCs while retaining one router.
post_execution_answers.decision: Accept bounded complexity increase, not arbitrary growth.

post_execution_answers.answer: Only the query contracts and typed result-product contracts are implemented in Phase 2. Projection/build execution remains Phase 3.
post_execution_answers.decision: Mark backend projection layer planned and never claim products are buildable yet.
post_execution_answers.acceptance_impact: Supports A2.8 and prevents capability overclaiming.

post_execution_answers.answer: No. All 47 v1.10 routing fixtures were preserved with zero regressions, and GP01–GP06 remained green.
post_execution_answers.decision: Accept new query routing only after legacy route preservation is demonstrated.

notes: Completed phase; questions reconstructed from the actual command/query design decisions. Q2.E1 records the acceptance-time compatibility question.
